questions.q: Where does Delegated Administration live in Setup?
options: In the Security Controls section, alongside Sharing Settings and Session Settings
Inside Object Manager, under each object's Field Dependencies page
Inside the Profiles list, as a checkbox on each profile
In the App Manager, as a type of connected app
questions.explain: Delegated Administration is found in Setup's Security Controls section, the same area as Sharing Settings and Session Settings — reflecting that it's a security boundary.

questions.q: What does 'Enable Group for Login Access' control on a Delegated Group?
options: Whether the group's members can reset their own passwords
Whether the group is visible to standard users
Whether the group's members can log in as the users they administer
Whether the group can create new profiles
questions.explain: Enable Group for Login Access lets members of the delegated group log in as the users within their scope — a significant permission worth granting deliberately.

questions.q: A newly created Delegated Group has just been saved. What can its members do at that point?
options: Everything a System Administrator can do, until scoped down
Nothing — every related list (Delegated Administrators, User Administration, Assignable Profiles, etc.) starts empty
Only reset passwords for users in their own role
Only view reports, until a profile is assigned to the group
questions.explain: The Delegated Group Detail page's five related lists all start empty — the group can do nothing until each one is deliberately filled in.

questions.q: Why does Assignable Profiles matter even after a delegated admin already has permission to create and edit users?
options: It doesn't matter — User Administration alone is sufficient
It determines how many users a delegated admin can create per day
It only controls which reports a delegated admin can run
Because creating a user requires assigning a profile, and without this limit a delegated admin could assign System Administrator and defeat the whole point of delegating
questions.explain: User Administration grants the ability to create/edit users, but creating a user means picking a profile — Assignable Profiles is the explicit, limited list of profiles a delegated admin is allowed to hand out.

questions.q: What is the underlying reason delegated administration is considered safer than handing out the System Administrator profile for routine tasks?
options: It limits the blast radius of a mistake or compromised account by scoping exactly what a delegated admin can touch
It requires two-factor authentication for every action
It automatically expires after 90 days
It prevents delegated admins from ever creating new users
questions.explain: The lesson frames delegated administration as limiting the blast radius — a delegated admin scoped to one role hierarchy, a couple of profiles, and a few custom objects simply can't reach what a full System Administrator can.
